paragraphs: H = our equity, also (1-V) L = amount lost V = opponent(s) equity, also (1-H)

This is the same way Derric Heynie describes fold equity in his book Quantum Poker: Summing Up Everything You will Ever Need to Know About Poker. To solve the example above, all we need to do is input the variables and estimate how often Villain is folding. Let's say we think Villain is folding 40% of the time.
X = folding frequency = 40% or 0.4 P = pot size = $100 W = net profit = $200 H = our equity = 20% or 0.2 L = amount lost = $100 V = opponent(s) equity = 80% or 0.8

On average you will profit $16 each time you shove if your opponent is folding 40% of the time. Now let me explain how we find the breakeven point. We simply change the expected value from the last equation to zero and solve for X.
